label: KMT2A::AFDN

sections.text: KMT2A encodes a chromatin regulator that controls developmental and hematopoietic transcription, including HOX genes.
AFDN encodes afadin, an actin-binding scaffold at cell-cell junctions.

The fusion retains the amino-terminal KMT2A chromatin-targeting and menin-interaction region while replacing its normal carboxy terminus. The altered complex sustains HOXA/MEIS1-associated self-renewal programs and drives acute leukemia. For this partner, the fusion represents a gain of leukemogenic transcriptional function rather than simple loss of the native partner.
KMT2A::AFDN has been associated with particularly poor event-free survival in pediatric AML cohorts.

Revumenib is US-approved for relapsed or refractory acute leukemia with a KMT2A translocation in adults and children aged at least 1 year. This indication targets the menin-dependent KMT2A fusion class.
